newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas seeks global impact after record net.
newsitem.headline: Petronas seeks global impact after record net.

text.p: Malaysia's state oil firm Petroliam Nasional (Petronas) reported a record profit on Thursday and said it aims to become a leading global multinational as oil reserves decline at home.
Petronas reported its net profit rose 48.3 percent to 6.76 billion ringgit ($2.6 billion) for the financial year ended March 31, 1996, on turnover of 22.25 billion ringgit.
"It's been a busy year and a quite successful year in terms of activities and financial performance," said Hassan Merican, who took over as Petronas president at the start of this year.

But the former finance manager had disappointing news for the company's foreign partners, saying the standard production sharing contract (PSC) would not be changed, despite earlier indications new incentives might be offered.
"We said we would review it. We have reviewed it and we're not going to change it," he said.
The PSC calls for an 80-20 split in Petronas' favour after costs are deducted. "It's tough but fair," Hassan said.
Petronas' new Yankee bond issue would be launched in the last week of September or the first week of October, he said.
The amount and tenure of the bond -- the company's third overseas bond issue -- will depend on the response of investors to a roadshow promoting the issue.
Hassan said he did not expect the issue to be affected by possible U.S. sanctions arising from Petronas' investment in Iran's Sirri oil fields.

Last month Petronas took a 30 percent stake in two Iranian oil fields being developed by Total SA of France. The investment in the $600 million project puts Malaysia in jeopardy of sanctions from the United States under the Iran-Libya Sanctions Act, signed by President Bill Clinton last month.
Hassan said the company has been given legal advice that any sanctions would not affect the bond issue.
In the meantime, Petronas has embarked upon a stepped up exploration programme at home and abroad. It has budgeted 6.0 billion ringgit for exploration work in the current year.
"Petronas is gearing up for a new direction in pursuit of its goal to become a leading oil and gas multinational of choice," Hassan said.
Petronas is producing oil from Vietnam's Dai Hung field and has made "considerable commercial discoveries" at its Emerald, Ruby and Topaz fields offshore Vung Tau, Vietnam, he said.
Petronas also signed oil and gas exploration contracts in the Philippines and Pakistan over the last year and an agreement with India would be announced in November, Hassan said.
In March, Petronas signed a deal with Indian Oil Corporation to make petroleum products.
Other foreign downstream ventures include a 30 percent ownership stake in a consortium with Conoco to build a 130,000 barrel a day refinery in Dung Quat, Vietnam, Hassan said.
Petronas has set up ventures in Vietnam, the Philippines and China to import and market liquefied petroleum gas.

It has expanded a chain of petrol stations in Cambodia to 10 and formed a joint venture with Unique Gas & Petrochemcials Plc to develop a network of service stations in Thailand under the Petronas brand name, Hassan said. ($1 = 2.4985 ringgit)
